questions.question: Which language should the Next.js portfolio use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Adds static typing and editor support; recommended for a maintainable portfolio.

options.label: JavaScript
options.description: Uses standard JavaScript with a simpler setup.

questions.rationale: The workspace is a TypeScript exercise and the request asks for a Next.js project.

questions.question: Which framework should power the portfolio frontend?

options.label: Next.js
options.description: React framework with file-based routes and support for optimized images.

options.label: Other
options.description: Choose or describe another frontend framework.

questions.rationale: The request explicitly asks to initialize a Next.js project.

questions.question: What portfolio content or interactions should the site include beyond the requested Home, About, Projects, and Contact pages?
questions.recommendedChoice: Placeholder frontend developer portfolio content with a modern dark visual style; use creative judgment for layout and details.
questions.answer: Use placeholders for a frontend developer portfolio. Choose a modern dark visual style and be creative.
questions.rationale: The user confirmed placeholder portfolio content, a modern dark visual direction, and creative discretion.

questions.question: Does the portfolio need persistent storage, file storage, a queue, or a cache?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: The portfolio is a static/client-rendered site and does not persist user or application data.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Stores portfolio images, documents, or other uploaded/served media.

questions.rationale: No backend, persistence, or upload workflow was requested; images can be stored as project assets.

questions.question: Will users sign in to use application features?

options.label: No
options.description: The portfolio is public and does not have sign-in protected application features.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users sign in to access application features.

questions.rationale: A public portfolio site with no authenticated application features was requested.
